fr: tremper dans la pâte à frire

does: Dips food in a thin, wet mixture of flour and cold liquid, so that it fries with a light, crisp, airy coat that is lighter than a crumb coat.
how: Stir the flour into cold liquid just until it is smooth enough to coat a spoon. A few lumps do no harm.
Keep the batter cold and use it soon after it is made.
Dry the food and dust it with a little flour so that the batter clings.
Dip the food, lift it and let the extra run off, then lower it into the hot oil away from you.
Fry in small batches so that the oil stays hot, and lift each piece out onto a rack.

cues.text: The batter coats a spoon in a thin even film and runs off in a slow stream.
The coat sizzles at once and bubbles as it meets the oil.

mistakes.mistake: Beating the batter smooth, which builds toughness into the coat.
mistakes.fix: Stir only until the flour has just gone in.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the batter stand warm for long, so that it turns heavy.
mistakes.fix: Keep it cold and make it just before frying.

mistakes.mistake: Frying too many pieces at once, so that the oil cools and the coat turns greasy.
mistakes.fix: Fry a few at a time.

comes_after.why: A batter is mixed with a quick whisk, so a cook has to know how far to take it.
